== Biography ==
'''Jane Glasgow''' was born about 1835 in County Antrim, Ireland. The surviving 1851 census records her as the sixteen-year-old daughter of [[Glasgow-1387|William Glasgow]] in his Cloughgaldenagh household. William's wife [[Unknown-540868|Ellin Glasgow]] was also present, and both spouses reported 1831 as the year of their first marriage.<ref name="Census1851">[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Killcondray/Dunaghy/Galdernaugh/1/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Galdernaugh/Cloughgaldenagh household 1, William Glasgow household.</ref>

Jane was a weaver and was recorded as born in County Antrim.<ref name="Census1851" />== Research Notes ==

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1387]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The detailed 1851 Cloughgaldenagh transcription identifies Jane Glasgow among William and wife Ellin’s eight children. Jane16 is recorded alive in 1851; selected 1841 death and Scottish birthplace are conflicting vitals, not contrary father evidence. Her biography already distinguishes the Scottish Jane Allan Glasgow-2082; the retained old Scottish vital fields are pending correction and do not define this Irish census child.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Check the full 1851 original relationship column and reconcile the child’s retained vitals.

Source basis already held: [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf “1851 Irish Census Returns,” Cloughgaldenagh house 1, Dunaghy, County Antrim, detailed public transcription, PDF (); see also National Archives of Ireland household page () and FamilySearch QV9Y-WFJ7]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



This profile formerly contained structured dates and a Scottish birthplace belonging to [[Glasgow-2082|Jane Allan Glasgow]], daughter of [[Glasgow-424|John Glasgow]] and [[Forsyth-878|Christina Forsyth]]. That separate Scottish profile preserves the earlier identity. The 1851 census proves that this Jane was alive in County Antrim and therefore could not have died before the 1841 Scottish census.
The GRONI index lists a Jane Glasgow–Lough marriage on 9 December 1868 in the Ballymena district; its connection to this profile remains open.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 9 December 1868, Ballymena district, M/1868/H1/233/13/289.</ref>
